correctness.rationale: Distinct nonempty maps have unique left shifts; idempotents form a Boolean semilattice. A two-state transfer matrix with row sum 2+z gives the crossing rank polynomial; summing over shifts proves the exact binomial coefficient. The disjoint local-indicator equations for all other shift pairs hold with probability at most 3/4 per selected independent site; a geometric shift tail gives the quantitative all-n bound. Standalone checker independently enumerated all n<=8 maps and compositions, verified the 4^n idempotent-core count and all crossing coefficients.

value.rationale: The global commuting probability and the rank-resolved first non-idempotent layer are intrinsic, motivated invariants for a recently investigated chain-isometry monoid. The 1/4 law and stretched-exponential idempotent domination distinguish this from nearby interval-restricted translation monoids, and the full crossing rank law yields a conditioned binomial distribution for all chain sizes. It is an infinite-family structural census, not an arbitrary finite slice.
